source.title: LionVote: Per-Layer Learning Rate Adaptation for Lion

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports training accuracies and optimizer comparisons, but not training classification error or whether models reach zero or near-zero training error. Its evidence does not test any listed version's claimed behavior.
record.gate_note: Reported validation accuracies, training-loss descriptions, and layer-wise optimizer diagnostics are not results on training classification error. The training-loss figures are described qualitatively, without reported numerical training-error results.
record.test_reason: No own result tests V1–V6. Appendix A.4 uses the cited edge-of-stability principle as a consistency check for LionVote's learning-rate multiplier, without measuring sharpness or stability thresholds. The experiments compare optimizers' validation performance and layer diagnostics; training-loss descriptions do not establish near-zero training classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report layer-dependent joint learning-rate and weight-decay scaling under LionVote, task-dependent benefits on ViT-Tiny, and dominant validation performance from tuned SGD on WideResNet. Their conclusion links adaptation value to architectural heterogeneity, but §5.2 explicitly notes that comparable heterogeneity accompanies opposite accuracy effects on the two CIFAR tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a per-layer adaptive learning-rate mechanism for Lion and reports validation accuracy; it does not evaluate the recipes or training-error measure in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and task affect validation-accuracy outcomes; voting cadence and update variant also affect reported validation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD achieves the highest validation accuracy on both WideResNet configurations: 96.08% on CIFAR-10 and 82.76% on CIFAR-100 (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects validation accuracy in these WideResNet recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: LionVote c8 improves ViT-Tiny validation accuracy over Lion on CIFAR-100 (69.71% versus 68.95%) but reduces it on CIFAR-10 (91.52% versus 92.40%; Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The validation-accuracy benefit of LionVote depends on the task.

fits_no_version.finding: LionVote assigns normalization parameters approximately 32–33% higher effective multipliers than attention parameters on ViT-Tiny/CIFAR-100. These multipliers scale both learning rate and weight decay (§5.1; Appendix B.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LionVote produces layer-type differences in joint learning-rate and weight-decay scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 describes faster training-loss convergence for adaptive optimizers than SGD on ViT-Tiny, and lower final training loss for SGD on WideResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects training-loss convergence under the tested recipes.

record.problems: The study's scope is limited to CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, WideResNet and ViT-Tiny, with 8 seeds per configuration. Some diagnostic comparisons are single-seed; the authors note cadence selection is partially post-hoc and that the study is underpowered below Cohen's d ≈ 0.8. Training-error outcomes are not reported in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: none of the reported outcomes measures training classification error or the other behavior named in V1–V6.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including corrupted or random labels, and its dependence on model size, early stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization comparisons measuring signal propagation, training speed or trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Matched normalization comparisons measuring training speed or learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for V1–V6. Validation accuracy, epochs to validation thresholds, gradient-alignment statistics and compound levels cannot substitute for the behaviors these versions specify. The record's relation='tests' conflicts with its own explanation and should be corrected.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training classification error, random or corrupted labels, or smaller-model/early-stopping training-error outcomes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width comparison is tested.
No comparison of plain and identity-shortcut networks' training error as depth increases is reported.
The study does not compare initialization schemes or test their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
The study does not test above-stability learning rates, curvature dynamics, or edge-of-stability behavior.
Although WRN models use BatchNorm, the study does not compare the same networks with and without normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
